input.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: The increases in average price per ad in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools.
Average price per ad in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 14% year-over-year.

input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Meta's Q3 2026 results show AI investments are improving advertising performance. This is an interpretive claim about causation/attribution rather than a purely numeric claim.

Evidence E1 directly supports this claim by stating that increases in average price per ad in Q3 2026 (the three months ended September 30, 2026) were "driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools." While the evidence doesn't explicitly use the term "AI investments," ad targeting and measurement tools are the specific advertising technologies that Meta has been investing in through AI, and the filing attributes the improved ad performance to these tools.

Evidence E2 confirms that average price per ad increased 14% year-over-year in Q3 2026, demonstrating the improved advertising performance referenced in the claim.

The evidence affirmatively establishes that Meta's Q3 2026 results show improvements in advertising performance (14% increase in average price per ad) and that these improvements are attributed to enhancements in ad targeting and measurement tools, which aligns with the claim about AI investments improving advertising performance.
